;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Christchurch mosque shootings]], [[Terrorism in New Zealand]]
**At least 50 people are killed and dozens others are injured during two attacks on mosques in [[Christchurch]], [[New Zealand]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/new-zealand-shooting-death-toll-rises-50-attack-mosque-n984066 (NBC News)]
**Four people—three men and one woman—are arrested in connection to the shootings, according to [[New Zealand Police]] Commissioner Mike Bush. It is later learned that one of them was an armed citizen trying to help police and was released. [https://news.sky.com/story/live-significant-number-killed-in-shootings-at-new-zealand-mosques-11665829 (Sky News)]
**A gunman involved in the shootings of at least one of the two mosques is identified as Brenton Tarrant, a 28-year-old [[Australian New Zealanders|Australian]] man. [https://apnews.com/1e19fefcb2e948a1bf7ce63429bc186e (Associated Press)]
*[[2019 Tel Aviv rocket strike]]
**In response to a possible accidental launching of two rockets from the [[Gaza Strip]] towards [[Tel Aviv]] the day before, Israel launches hundreds of counter strikes directed at the town of [[Khan Yunis]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/14/world/israel-reports-rocket-attack-on-tel-aviv.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/israeli-military-announces-strikes-gaza-sites-after-rocket-attack-tel-n983551 (Associated Press)]
;Health and environment
*[[School strike for climate]]
**Hundreds of thousands of students protest worldwide for [[climate change mitigation]]. [http://www.ansa.it/english/news/general_news/2019/03/15/italian-climate-protesters-demand-action_dc295006-6a6a-4062-ac72-29f15a28c9d7.html (ANSA)] [https://www.archynewsy.com/climate-events-all-over-the-world-students-invade-the-squares-in-italy-we-are-one-million/ (Archynewsy.com)] [https://www.smh.com.au/education/don-t-want-the-earth-to-get-hurt-150-000-students-strike-20190315-p514ky.html (''The Sydney Morning Herald'')]
*[[Keystone_Pipeline|Keystone pipeline]] expansion
**A U.S. appeals court denies [[TransCanada Corporation|TransCanada's]] request to lift an injunction preventing pre-construction work on the Keystone XL expansion from beginning. The company claims this will delay the project by a year. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/transcanada-keystone-pipeline-1.5058988 (CBC)]

;International relations 
*[[United States and the International Criminal Court]], [[United States war crimes]], [[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)#War crimes|War crimes in Afghanistan]]
**[[United States Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] bars the entry of [[International Criminal Court]] investigators into the United States as part of the ICC's investigation into possible [[War crime|war crimes]] committed by [[United States Armed Forces|the United States military]] in [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.apnews.com/08e538e370914f6e8243e237dbde50b5 (Associated Press)]
*[[North Korea and weapons of mass destruction]], [[North Korea–United States relations]]
**[[North Korea]] has reportedly threatened to suspend negotiations with the [[United States]] regarding nuclear weaponry, as well as resume related missile testing. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/15/world/asia/north-korea-kim-jong-un-nuclear.html (''The New York Times'')]
;Law and crime
*[[Volkswagen emissions scandal]]
**The [[Securities and Exchange Commission]] alleges in a court filing that [[Volkswagen]] has "perpetrated a massive fraud" and repeatedly lied to U.S. investors in connection with diesel emissions. [https://www.cnbc.com/2019/03/15/dieselgate-sec-says-volkswagen-perpetrated-fraud-lied-to-investors.html (CNBC)]
;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Algerian protests]]
**The 2019 Algerian protests, the largest protests since the [[Algerian Civil War]], have led the government to cancel the Presidential elections, to replace the Prime Minister, and to promise [[Abdelaziz Bouteflika]] would not run for re-election. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/why-algeria-is-still-protesting-after-ruler-relents/2019/03/13/e5353bb2-455d-11e9-94ab-d2dda3c0df52_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[National Emergency Concerning the Southern Border of the United States]]
** [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] issues his first ever veto after Congress attempts to block his emergency declaration to fund construction of the [[Trump wall|wall]] along the [[Mexico–United States border]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/15/us/politics/trump-veto-national-emergency.html (''The New York Times'')]
*Lawmakers in [[Mexico]]'s [[Chamber of Deputies (Mexico)|lower chamber of Congress]] approve a constitutional reform that would allow for [[Recall election|recall referendums]] to cut short the six-year presidential term limit; the measure still needs the approval of the [[Senate of Mexico|Senate]] and the state legislatures. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-politics/mexicos-lower-house-passes-measure-to-cut-short-presidential-term-idUSKCN1QW0FC (Reuters)]
